Whether the transition is active. When false, the items it animates change instantly.
Read-only: true while the transition is playing on at least one series.
Share of duration over which the start times of the items are spread, in [0, 1].

detaileddescription.para: 0 animates all items together; 1 animates them one after another, each changing at once. Items start in index order. Values outside [0, 1] are clamped. Default: 0, and 1 for DrawTransition.

briefdescription.para: Qt Quick animations of the opacity of each item, such as NumberAnimation { property: "opacity" }.

detaileddescription.para: The default property. The animations run together on the timeline of each item, which starts when the item starts to move. They are read, never run, so running, paused, and their signals have no effect.

listitem.para: Supported: NumberAnimation and other numeric PropertyAnimation types, PropertyAction, PauseAnimation, SequentialAnimation, and ParallelAnimation, with finite loops.
A missing from continues from the opacity reached so far, and a missing to is 1. Before its first animation starts, an item shows that animation's start opacity.
Other animations, such as SpringAnimation or ScriptAction, and animations of other properties log a warning and only add their duration.
When the animations last longer than an item's share of duration, the start times of the items move closer together, so the transition still ends after duration.
The opacity is clamped to [0, 1], and every item is opaque again when the transition ends.

Abstract base class for animated data transitions on plot series.

detaileddescription.para: A series animates a data change with up to three transitions, matched to its items by index: enterTransition for added items, updateTransition for kept items, and exitTransition for removed items. MorphTransition, DrawTransition, and GrowTransition are the available transitions.

Time comes from Qt's animation timer on the transition's thread, the clock of QML animations. An installed QAnimationDriver therefore steps transitions too, for example to record frames offscreen at a fixed time step.
One transition can be assigned to several series, and to several slots of one series. Each assignment keeps its own Run, so the animations are independent.
